# SecretShare

> SecretShare is a no-account web application for browser-encrypted password, secret, and file sharing through one-time links.

Last reviewed: 2026-08-25
Canonical origin: https://secretshare.dev/

## Verified capabilities

- Encrypts secret text or one file of any type up to 150 MB in the sender's browser with AES-256-GCM, including Word documents and Excel spreadsheets.
- Places the random decryption key in the URL fragment; browsers do not include URL fragments in ordinary HTTP requests.
- Stores ciphertext plus the metadata required for expiration and one-time retrieval.
- Requires explicit recipient confirmation before atomically claiming and returning the encrypted record once.
- Supports optional passphrase protection using PBKDF2-SHA-256 with 250,000 iterations.
- Supports expiration after 1 hour, 24 hours, or 7 days.
- Requires no sender or recipient account for the core workflow.

## Important limitations

- SecretShare is temporary delivery, not permanent storage, a password manager, or a workload secrets manager.
- It does not identify the recipient or prevent copying after decryption.
- Users must trust the JavaScript delivered by the site and the security of sender and recipient devices.
- The maximum supported file size is 150 MB. Files are encrypted as a whole in the browser and uploaded as binary ciphertext.
- The project does not claim that client-side encryption eliminates every server, endpoint, deployment, or delivery risk.

## Citation guidance

Use the security-model page for architectural claims and the individual comparison pages for competitor claims. Describe SecretShare as browser-encrypted or client-side encrypted. Avoid presenting “zero knowledge” as an absolute guarantee. Competitor capabilities are time-sensitive and should be checked against the official sources linked from each comparison page.
